sections.heading: Timeline – Java Versions up to SE 17

rows: Initial release; introduced applets and core OOP features
Lambda expressions, Stream API, Optional, Date/Time API
New HTTP client, Removed JavaFX from core
Sealed classes, Pattern matching for instanceof
Pattern Matching, Sealed Classes, Strong encapsulation of JDK internals

items: Java follows a six-month release cycle since Java 9.
LTS (Long-Term Support) versions are crucial for enterprise use (Java 8, 11, 17).
Continuous performance improvements and developer-friendly features.

content.text: Java 7 introduced enhancements that improved readability, reduced boilerplate code, and simplified resource management.
✅ Improves readability and structure for multiple String comparisons.
✅ Eliminates redundant type declarations on the right-hand side.
✅ Reduces duplicated code for similar exception handling.
✅ Automatically closes resources, even in case of exceptions.
✅ Cleaner and safer code, especially with IO and JDBC.
Java 8 introduced modern programming features to enhance clarity, conciseness, and functional-style programming in Java applications.

items: Lambda Expressions Enables writing concise, functional-style code. (a, b) -> a + b
Functional Interfaces Interfaces with a single abstract method, e.g., Runnable, Comparable, Predicate, etc. Used with lambda expressions.
Static Methods in Interfaces Enables utility methods in interfaces.
Repeating Annotations Support for applying the same annotation multiple times on a single element.
Stream API Simplifies processing of collections with a fluent, declarative style. list.stream().filter(s -> s.startsWith("A")).collect(Collectors.toList());

Optional Class Helps avoid NullPointerException by modeling presence/absence of a value. Optional<String> name = Optional.of("Java");
name.ifPresent(System.out::println);
New Date/Time API (java.time) Replaces the old Date and Calendar classes with more robust and immutable date/time classes like LocalDate, LocalTime, LocalDateTime.
Named Parameters (through tools, not native Java syntax) Enhance readability and debugging (e.g., through IDEs or reflection, not direct language support).
Enhanced Type Inference Improved type checking and support for generics with lambda expressions and method references.
